threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it a 'notting hill' party instead of a 'house gathering' — makes it clear you’re not yet in the local groove.
Caught a guy in a flat cap trying to negotiate a deal for leftover chicken on the 133. The driver just shook his head, amused.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a street musician playing accordion for a group of toddlers dancing around a fountain in Hasenheide, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Späti that doubles as a mini art gallery, showcasing local artists’ work right next to the beer fridges.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know that the BART delays mean planning around the 24-hour taco spot, not just the train schedule. We adapt, they wait.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a suit feeding a pigeon while waiting for the bus. He looked more at peace than anyone on their phone around him.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all the locals flock to Park Güell, but on a sunny day, you’ll find us lounging in the secret corners of Plaça de la Vila.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they still search for the pause button on the metro when it stops unexpectedly. We're all used to it by now.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it the 'Overground' instead of the 'Ginger Line'—everyone here knows it's the one with the best street food nearby.
Last night, saw a guy serenading the bus with a ukulele. Got off at Stockwell, still strumming as he walked away, pure Brixton vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a couple casually fixing their bike in front of a café while a street artist painted a mural on the wall, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can order a beer at a kiosk in Friedrichshain at 8 AM, and no one bats an eye. It's a morning ritual for some locals.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their willingness to sprint for the 14 bus instead of waiting. It’s a trademark of survival here.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 31 doing yoga during rush hour. Only in San Francisco would a bumpy bus ride turn into a Zen moment. Totally unfazed.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every café has Wi-Fi. In Gràcia, a lot of locals prefer to connect over coffee, not the internet.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling with the T-10 tickets at the machines, while locals swipe their smartphones without a second thought.
